sections.summary: AI tools are expanding across healthcare, but adoption should be judged against clinical validation and governance evidence.
Nature's skin-cancer study shows image-classification promise while staying within visual dermatology tasks.
The JAMA diabetic-retinopathy validation study supports retinal-fundus-photo screening rather than broad clinical diagnosis.
FDA's AI-enabled device list provides regulatory transparency for authorized devices in the United States.
WHO guidance stresses ethics, human rights, accountability, and governance for AI in health.
Recommendation: prioritize validated, scoped diagnostic workflows and require post-deployment monitoring before scaling.
Appendix details include source collection notes and background definitions.
